name: Hachi-Hachi (八八)
description: Hachi-Hachi (八八, '88') is the most representative Japanese Hanafuda fishing game. The name refers to the par score of 88 points (one-third of the 264 total points in the deck). Played by 3-6 players with a bidding phase to determine the three active players each round. Features complex scoring with teyaku (initial hand combinations) and deki-yaku (combinations formed during play). Players can stop early if they form valuable combinations.

history.origins: Traditional Japanese game using Hanafuda (flower cards), which originated in the 18th century. Hachi-Hachi is considered the most representative Hanafuda fishing game.
timeline: 18th Century: Hanafuda cards introduced to Japan.
19th Century: Fishing games with Hanafuda develop.
20th Century: Hachi-Hachi becomes the standard Hanafuda game.
Present: Played throughout Japan and in Japanese communities worldwide.
history.cultural: Represents traditional Japanese card gaming culture. Hanafuda cards are iconic in Japan and used in various games.
history.evolution: Evolved from earlier Hanafuda fishing games, adding the bidding phase and complex yaku (scoring combinations) system.

setup.players: 3-6 players. Only 3 play actively each round; others sit out after bidding.
setup.dealing: Deal cards to the 3 active players. Place cards face-up in the center (the 'field').
setup.equipment: Two denominations of chips: 'Kan' and 'Mon' (1 Kan = 12 Mon typically).

rules.objective: Score as close to 88 points as possible (the par score). Players pay/receive based on deviation from 88. Alternatively, form valuable yaku combinations to stop play early and claim payment.
rules.gameplay: 1. Bidding Phase (if more than 3 players): Players bid to determine the 3 active players for the round. Non-active players sit out but may still earn from teyaku. 2. Dealing: Deal cards to the 3 active players. Place cards face-up in the center (the 'field'). 3. Playing Phase: Players take turns playing a card from hand to capture matching cards from the field. A card matches if it's from the same month/suit. After playing from hand, flip the top card from the deck. If it matches a field card, capture it. Captured cards go into the player's scoring pile. 4. Scoring: Total card points = 264 (par = 88 per player). Teyaku (Initial Hand Combinations): Declared before play for immediate payment. Deki-Yaku (Play Combinations): Formed during play. Player can stop early to claim payment. Final score = (Your points - 88). Positive = win, Negative = loss.
keyRules: The par score of 88 is key—aim to exceed it, not just maximize points.
Teyaku are initial hand combinations declared before play for immediate payment.
Deki-yaku are combinations formed during play; players can stop early to claim payment.
Cards match by month/suit (same month cards capture each other).
After playing from hand, flip top card from deck—if it matches field card, capture it.

strategy.basic: Focus on capturing high-value cards (Brights, Animals, Ribbons). Avoid letting opponents form yaku.
strategy.intermediate: Track which cards have been played to anticipate remaining cards. Decide whether to stop early with a yaku or continue playing for more points.
strategy.advanced: Calculate exact point differentials. Bluff during bidding to become an active player. Memorize all yaku and their values to maximize scoring opportunities.
tips: The par score of 88 is key—aim to exceed it, not just maximize points.
Stopping early with a yaku guarantees payment, but continuing might yield more.
In the bidding phase, assess your hand's potential before committing.
